title: Grain-free granola
summary: Clusters of toasted nuts, seeds and coconut bound with egg white and baked low so they crisp without burning.
steps: Heat the oven to 150 °C (300 °F) and line a large baking sheet with parchment.
Mix the nuts, coconut, seeds, flaxseed meal, erythritol, cinnamon and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk the egg white until frothy, then whisk in the coconut oil and vanilla. Pour over the dry mix and stir until everything is coated.
Spread in an even layer about 1 cm (½ in) thick and press down firmly with a spatula.
Bake 25–30 minutes, rotating the pan halfway, until golden. Coconut darkens fast at the end, so check from 20 minutes.
Let it cool completely on the pan without stirring — it crisps as it cools — then break into clusters. Store airtight up to 2 weeks.
tips: Serve with almond milk or coconut yogurt and a few berries.

origin.history: Granola began in American health reform. In 1863 James Caleb Jackson, who ran a sanatorium in Dansville, New York, made "granula" from baked whole-grain flour broken into pieces. John Harvey Kellogg later sold a similar product under the name granola, and the toasted oat-and-nut mix familiar today became popular in the 1960s.
